units.title: Unit 1: Cells, Organelles & Human Body Systems

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Cell Theory, Organelles & Plant vs. Animal Cells
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy Middle School Biology: Cells and Organelles
lessons.reading: All living things are composed of one or more cells—the basic unit of life. Inside eukaryotic cells, specialized organelles carry out vital functions: the nucleus stores DNA and directs cell activities; mitochondria perform cellular respiration to release ATP energy; the cell membrane regulates what enters and leaves; and plant cells additionally possess a rigid cell wall and chloroplasts for photosynthesis.

principles.title: Cell Organelles and Plant vs. Animal Cell Differences
principles.summary: Identify functions of the nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts, cell wall, and cell membrane.

bank.prompt: Which organelle is known as the "powerhouse of the cell" because it converts glucose into usable cellular energy (ATP)?
bank.answer: Mitochondria
bank.explanation: Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration, breaking down sugar molecules to release energy for the cell.

bank.prompt: Which two structures are present in PLANT cells but NOT in animal cells?
choices: Chloroplasts and a rigid cell wall
bank.answer: Chloroplasts and a rigid cell wall
bank.explanation: Plant cells have chloroplasts to capture sunlight for photosynthesis and a cellulose cell wall for structural support.

bank.prompt: What is the main role of the selectively permeable cell membrane?
choices: Controlling which substances enter and exit the cell to maintain homeostasis
Giving oak trees rigid woody bark
bank.answer: Controlling which substances enter and exit the cell to maintain homeostasis
bank.explanation: The cell membrane acts as a selective gatekeeper, letting nutrients and water in while exporting wastes.

bank.prompt: Where is the hereditary genetic material (DNA) housed in a eukaryotic cell?
bank.answer: Inside the nucleus
bank.explanation: In eukaryotic cells, chromosomes made of DNA are enclosed inside the membrane-bound nucleus.

bank.prompt: Which statement is a fundamental part of modern Cell Theory?
choices: All living organisms are made of one or more cells, and all cells come from pre-existing cells.
Only animals are made of cells; plants are made of minerals.
Cells spontaneously generate from nonliving dust every day.
All cells are large enough to see without a microscope.
bank.answer: All living organisms are made of one or more cells, and all cells come from pre-existing cells.
bank.explanation: Cell theory states that cells are the basic unit of life, all organisms consist of cells, and cells arise from existing cells.

bank.prompt: In what order is biological organization arranged from SIMPLEST to MOST COMPLEX in multicellular organisms?
choices: Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ System → Organism
Organ → Cell → Tissue → Organism → Organ System
Tissue → Cell → Organ System → Organ → Organism
Organism → Organ System → Organ → Tissue → Cell
bank.answer: Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ System → Organism
bank.explanation: Similar cells form tissues, tissues combine into organs, organs work together in organ systems, making up the organism.

bank.prompt: Why do plant cells have a single large central vacuole?
choices: To store water and maintain turgor pressure so the plant stays upright
To pump blood through the stem
To help the plant walk toward light
bank.answer: To store water and maintain turgor pressure so the plant stays upright
bank.explanation: When full of water, the central vacuole presses outward against the cell wall (turgor pressure), keeping stems crisp.

bank.prompt: How do the respiratory and circulatory systems work together in the human body?
choices: The lungs take in oxygen and transfer it to the blood, which the heart pumps to body cells.
The lungs pump blood while the heart digests food.
The circulatory system only carries carbon dioxide and never oxygen.
They operate completely independently without interacting.
bank.answer: The lungs take in oxygen and transfer it to the blood, which the heart pumps to body cells.
bank.explanation: Alveoli in the lungs diffuse oxygen into capillaries, and the cardiovascular system delivers that oxygen to every cell.

units.title: Unit 2: Plate Tectonics, Water Cycle & Thermal Energy Transfer

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Plate Tectonics, Convection Currents & Earth’s Interior
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy Earth Science: Plate Tectonics & Mantle Convection
lessons.reading: Earth’s rigid outer shell (the lithosphere) is broken into tectonic plates that float atop the hot, slowly flowing asthenosphere (upper mantle). Convection currents driven by heat from Earth’s core move these plates. Plates pull apart at divergent boundaries (creating mid-ocean ridges), collide at convergent boundaries (forming mountain ranges and subduction trenches), and slide past each other at transform boundaries (causing frequent earthquakes).

principles.title: Tectonic Plate Boundaries and Mantle Convection
principles.summary: Distinguish convergent, divergent, and transform boundaries and the role of mantle convection.

bank.prompt: What is the primary driving force that causes Earth’s tectonic plates to move slowly over millions of years?
choices: Convection currents of heated rock rising and cooler rock sinking in the mantle
Solar flares striking the North Pole
bank.answer: Convection currents of heated rock rising and cooler rock sinking in the mantle
bank.explanation: Heat from Earth’s core drives slow thermal convection currents in the mantle that drag tectonic plates along.

bank.prompt: At a DIVERGENT plate boundary on the ocean floor, two tectonic plates move apart and magma rises to form a:
choices: Mid-ocean ridge and new oceanic crust
bank.answer: Mid-ocean ridge and new oceanic crust
bank.explanation: Seafloor spreading at divergent boundaries creates underwater mountain chains called mid-ocean ridges.

bank.prompt: The Himalayan Mountains (including Mount Everest) formed when the Indian Plate collided head-on with the Eurasian Plate. What kind of boundary is this?
bank.answer: Convergent boundary
bank.explanation: When two continental plates collide at a convergent boundary, the crust buckles upward into towering mountain ranges.

bank.prompt: At the San Andreas Fault in California, two plates grind horizontally past each other in opposite directions, causing frequent earthquakes. This is a:
bank.answer: Transform boundary
bank.explanation: Plates sliding laterally past one another form a transform fault boundary.

bank.prompt: Which pieces of evidence did Alfred Wegener use to support his hypothesis of Continental Drift?
choices: Matching continental coastlines, identical fossils on separate continents, and matching rock formations
bank.answer: Matching continental coastlines, identical fossils on separate continents, and matching rock formations
bank.explanation: Wegener pointed to puzzle-like continent shapes (South America and Africa), Mesosaurus/Glossopteris fossils, and matching rock belts.

bank.prompt: When a dense oceanic plate collides with a less dense continental plate, the oceanic plate sinks beneath it into the mantle in a process called:
bank.answer: Subduction
bank.explanation: Denser oceanic lithosphere subducts beneath continental lithosphere, forming deep ocean trenches and volcanic arcs.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Thermal Energy Transfer (Conduction, Convection, Radiation) & Water Cycle
lessons.videoTitle: Thermal Energy Transfer & The Global Water Cycle
lessons.reading: Thermal energy always flows spontaneously from warmer objects to cooler objects by three mechanisms: Conduction (direct particle-to-particle contact, such as a metal spoon in hot soup), Convection (circulation of warm, less-dense fluids rising and cooler, denser fluids sinking in liquids and gases), and Radiation (electromagnetic waves traveling through space, such as sunlight warming Earth). Solar radiation and gravity together drive the global water cycle.

principles.title: Conduction, Convection, Radiation & Water Cycle Drivers
principles.summary: Identify conduction, convection, and radiation, and explain how solar energy and gravity power the water cycle.

bank.prompt: A metal spoon left resting in a pot of boiling soup quickly becomes hot at the handle. How did heat travel up the solid spoon?
bank.answer: Conduction
bank.explanation: Conduction transfers thermal energy through direct collisions between vibrating atoms in a solid.

bank.prompt: How does thermal energy from the Sun travel through the vacuum of outer space to warm Earth?
bank.answer: Radiation (electromagnetic waves)
bank.explanation: Only electromagnetic radiation can transfer energy across empty space without a matter medium.

bank.prompt: In a heated room or a pot of water on a stove, warm fluid becomes less dense and rises while cooler, denser fluid sinks. This circular transfer is:
bank.answer: Convection
bank.explanation: Convection is heat transfer by the bulk movement of fluids (liquids or gases) due to density differences.

bank.prompt: Which two fundamental forces/energy sources drive the continuous movement of water through Earth’s water cycle?
choices: Energy from the Sun (driving evaporation) and gravity (pulling precipitation and runoff down)
bank.answer: Energy from the Sun (driving evaporation) and gravity (pulling precipitation and runoff down)
bank.explanation: Solar radiation evaporates water into vapor, and gravity pulls condensed rain/snow back to Earth and down rivers.

bank.prompt: In which direction does thermal energy naturally flow when two objects at different temperatures touch?
choices: From the warmer object to the cooler object until they reach thermal equilibrium
From the colder object into the hotter object
Thermal energy never moves between objects
bank.answer: From the warmer object to the cooler object until they reach thermal equilibrium
bank.explanation: By the Second Law of Thermodynamics, heat flows spontaneously from higher temperature to lower temperature.

bank.prompt: Why do insulated thermoses and winter jackets use trapped air pockets or foam?
choices: Because trapped air is a thermal insulator that slows down heat transfer by conduction and convection
Because foam creates new heat out of nothing
Because metal conducts heat too slowly
bank.answer: Because trapped air is a thermal insulator that slows down heat transfer by conduction and convection
bank.explanation: Insulators resist thermal energy flow, keeping hot drinks hot and body heat inside.

lessons.title: Unit 2 Exam: Earth Systems & Thermal Energy
lessons.reading: Review plate tectonics, thermal transfer, and the water cycle for the Unit 2 Exam.

principles.title: Tectonic Plate Boundaries and Mantle Convection
principles.summary: Analyze geological features formed at plate boundaries.

bank.prompt: New oceanic crust is continuously created by rising magma at which tectonic feature?
bank.answer: Mid-ocean ridges (divergent boundaries)
bank.explanation: At divergent boundaries underwater, plates pull apart and magma solidifies into new oceanic crust.

bank.prompt: Why are most of the world’s active volcanoes and earthquakes concentrated along the "Ring of Fire" around the Pacific Ocean?
choices: It traces the boundaries where the Pacific Plate converges and subducts beneath surrounding plates.
The equator runs in a circle around the Pacific.
Meteorites strike the Pacific shoreline more often.
Ocean water is warmer near volcanoes.
bank.answer: It traces the boundaries where the Pacific Plate converges and subducts beneath surrounding plates.
bank.explanation: Active subduction zones around the Pacific Rim generate intense seismic and volcanic activity.

bank.prompt: Which layer of Earth is composed of hot, semi-solid rock that flows slowly by convection?
bank.answer: The mantle (asthenosphere)
bank.explanation: The mantle lies beneath the crust and convects slowly over geologic time.

principles.title: Conduction, Convection, Radiation & Water Cycle Drivers
principles.summary: Apply thermal transfer concepts and water cycle mechanics.

bank.prompt: As water vapor rises high into the cooler troposphere, it cools and changes from a gas into tiny liquid cloud droplets. This process is:
bank.answer: Condensation
bank.explanation: Cooling water vapor loses thermal energy and condenses into liquid droplets that form clouds.

bank.prompt: A sea breeze blows from the cool ocean toward the warm land during a sunny afternoon primarily because of:
choices: Convection: air over the warm land heats up, becomes less dense, and rises, drawing cooler ocean air inward
bank.answer: Convection: air over the warm land heats up, becomes less dense, and rises, drawing cooler ocean air inward
bank.explanation: Unequal heating of land and water creates a convection cell known as a sea breeze.

bank.prompt: Which material is the BEST thermal conductor for cooking food quickly on a stove?
bank.answer: Copper or aluminum metal
bank.explanation: Metals have free-moving electrons that transfer thermal energy rapidly by conduction.
